issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares the lecture attributes as private ('-lectureName', '-numberOfInscribedStudents', etc.), and the solution implements them as private fields. However, the template Lecture.java exposes some attributes as public (e.g., public String lectureName; public int numberOfInscribedStudents;). This visibility mismatch between the problem specification and the template can confuse students about the intended access level and whether they should implement getters/setters or keep fields public.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template match the UML/specification by declaring the attributes as private and add the missing attributes as private as well (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). Alternatively, if the intent is to have public fields, update the UML and problem description to show public visibility. Prefer changing the template to private fields so students implement the requested getters/setters as described.
